case_text:
Vignette:
A 19-year-old tall, thin male (6'3", 145 lbs) presents with sudden onset of sharp right-sided pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea that began 2 hours ago while playing basketball. He has no prior medical history, takes no medications, and does not smoke. On examination, he is mildly tachypneic but speaking in full sentences. Vital signs: T 36.8C, HR 104, RR 22, BP 128/76, SpO2 93% on room air. The right hemithorax is hyperresonant to percussion with decreased breath sounds on the right compared to the left. Chest X-ray reveals a large right-sided pneumothorax with approximately 60% lung collapse and no mediastinal shift. There is no evidence of pleural effusion.
